comparison: Perfect agreement on C9 (methodological innovation). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the novelty claim would benefit from more comprehensive literature review, while peer reviewers accept the innovation without challenge as part of 'compelling evidence.'

Perfect agreement on C17-C24 (GO term enrichment analysis). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the inference about ATP production is interpretive but reasonable, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'global approach' demonstrating systemic-level insights.

Perfect agreement on C29-C32, C74-C75 (FtsZ/FtsA targeting). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the concentration-dependent effects and validation with prior literature, while peer reviewers accept this as 'compelling evidence' within the multi-omics framework.

Disagreement on C33-C34 (Tig targeting). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to authors' acknowledgment of potential noise and need for further investigation. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, accepting PISA-based identification without addressing the uncertainty.

Perfect agreement on C54-C68 (WGCNA results). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes methodological soundness and systems-level understanding, while peer reviewers praise this as exemplifying 'how the development of sensitive data analysis is still a major necessity.'

Perfect agreement on C69-C72 (PISA-WGCNA integration). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the multi-omics integration linking targets to network effects, while peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating how similar molecules 'act differently within the context of the whole set of cellular transcripts.'

Perfect agreement on C76-C79 (ATP-synthase targeting). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of target identification and functional validation, while peer reviewers accept this as 'compelling evidence through multi-omics and functional approaches.'

Perfect agreement on C86-C88 (DNA damage pathway). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the convergence of transcriptomics/proteomics, PISA, and TUNEL assay, while peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive mechanistic characterization.

Disagreement on C89-C91 (metabolic effects). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to authors' explicit statement about 'poor signal-to-noise ratio' in OCR data. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, stating experiments are 'well designed' without addressing the acknowledged data quality issues.

Strong agreement on C10-C14 (transcriptomics/proteomics scale and coverage). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive data and appropriate statistical analysis, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'well designed' experiments. Peer result also includes C15 (IVk anomaly) which OpenEval addresses separately in R6.

Agreement on C82-C85 (ROS generation). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the structure-activity relationship but acknowledges debate about ROS's causal role in bactericidal activity. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting mechanistic understanding without addressing the field debate. Peer result excludes C92 (literature context).

Agreement on C52-C53, C81 (flavodoxin target validation). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this validates the PISA approach despite lack of statistical significance for some compounds. Peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating 'robustness of experimental strategy.' Peer result excludes C80.

Agreement on C1-C4 (background/rationale). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations to peer-reviewed literature, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these claims without challenge. Peer result also includes C5-C6 which OpenEval addresses in R2.

Strong agreement on C25-C28 (CagA targeting). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes functional consequences require validation, while peer reviewers accept this as 'compelling evidence.' Peer result also includes C73 (summary of virulence factor targeting) which OpenEval addresses separately in R18. Both exclude C95 (biological context).

Partial agreement on essential protein targets. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on C48-C51 (unique targets per compound), while peer reviewers address broader set C45-C51 (including PISA screening methodology). Both accept the diversity of targets and pathway-specific identification.

Partial agreement on antimicrobial spectra. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C7-C8, C93-C94 (chemical structures and spectra), while peer reviewers focus only on C93-C94. Both accept the differential activity of structurally similar compounds.

Partial agreement on compound characterization. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C7-C8, C93-C94 (structures and spectra), while peer reviewers focus only on C7-C8 (structures). Both accept the structural characterization as part of experimental framework.

Partial agreement on methodological and mechanistic interpretation. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C96-C97 (PISA capabilities), while peer reviewers address C95-C98 (including virulence factor context and systemic regulation). Both accept the interpretive framework.

Partial overlap on essential genes and literature context. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C41-C47 (essential gene screening and targets), while peer reviewers address C16, C41-C44, C80, C92, C99 (essential genes plus various literature-supported contextual claims). Both accept these as valid scientific framework.

Minimal overlap on background claims. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C5-C6, C53 (flavodoxin rationale and drug discovery role), while peer reviewers address C1-C6 (broader background including H. pylori context). Both accept the background as appropriately documented.

Minimal overlap on systemic regulation interpretation. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C98 (type IV secretion system inference), while peer reviewers address C95-C98 (broader mechanistic insights). Both accept the network-based interpretations.

Minimal overlap on virulence factor targeting. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C73 (summary of CagA targeting), while peer reviewers address C25-C28, C73 (detailed PISA results plus summary). Both accept this as significant therapeutic finding.

Minimal overlap on IVk anomaly. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C15-C16 (transcriptional-translational decoupling), while peer reviewers address C10-C15 (omics coverage plus IVk anomaly). Both accept the anomalous observation with appropriate literature context.

OpenEval addresses C40 (IVk negative PISA results) and evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting this is consistent with IVk's anomalous behavior. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific negative result.
